turns.teacher: Hi, Mahi! Today we’ll use magnets to find directions, like finding your way on a nature walk. If a bar magnet hangs freely from a thread, which way do you think its ends will point when it stops?

ask.text: A bar magnet hangs freely from a thread. When it stops moving, in which directions do its ends point?

screen.ask: A bar magnet hangs freely from a thread. When it stops moving, in which directions do its ends point?

child.say: north and south... I think. Yeh toh easy hai, magnet hamesha north-south mein rukta hai.
child.private: knows the answer pattern, wants to look smart, but doesn't really get why
child.sent: north and south... I think. Yeh toh easy hai, magnet hamesha north-south mein rukta hai.

turns.teacher: Yes, tum got it: the hanging magnet settles roughly north to south. Its north-pointing end is called the north pole. Earth acts like a giant magnet and guides it. If Golu says the needle points north because the North Pole is cold, what is wrong with that idea?

ask.text: Golu says: 'A compass needle points north because it is so cold at the North Pole, and magnets like cold.' What is wrong?

screen.ask: Golu says: 'A compass needle points north because it is so cold at the North Pole, and magnets like cold.' What is wrong?

child.private: Trying to deny the cold idea but can't explain why properly. Knows magnets don't care about cold but can't connect Earth's magnetism clearly.

child.private: Trying to sound smart. I know magnets push or pull, but not sure which happens to a compass needle.
child.sent: Needle hategi... it will move, towards the magnet maybe? Because magnet attracts iron... but compass needle bhi magnet hai na? Toh... either attract karega ya push karega.

ask.text: Your compass needle has settled. How do you find east?

child.sent: North? Because needle ka N end counter ki taraf point kar raha hai... but needle toh magnet hai na? Toh north-pointing end north ki taraf hi hota hai usually... I am confused.

child.sent: North... I think. Counter is north.

child.sent: Wooden table wala... because steel almirah mein magnet lag sakta hai, aur fir needle idhar-udhar hoga. Toh table wala sahi hoga.

learning.why: Teacher explained that metal or magnets nearby can mess up a compass; now I get that steel can also affect it.

end.summary:
Practised how a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north–south.
Discussed using a compass to identify north, east, and west.
Explored why magnets and nearby steel or magnets can affect a compass needle.
Mahi explained that a rubbed paper clip can settle north–south like a compass.
The teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Mahi practised finding directions with a compass and explaining why a magnet settles north–south. They used the method of finding north first, then locating east to the right and west to the left; an earlier mix-up about directions was corrected by the end of the lesson (correctAfterLastSeen). At home, ask Mahi to place a compass flat away from metal objects, wait for the needle to settle, and name north, east, south, and west.
